entry.title: Problem with discarding entity using CAP as a proxy of RAP V4 Service
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

i've built an App on the Public Cloud, using RAP V4 Service for data persistence and also using determinations, validations etc.
I'm then using a CAP Service to add custom functionality with accessing external/SAP API's. I added my RAP V4 Service using basic entity projection and a little more complicated event handlers. Most of it works good when consumed by Fiori Elements App, but i am facing an issue, where i discard the entity i am editing (not when creating), it successfully discard its, but then fails to read and rebind to the "active" Entity.

 

From the UI Console and Network Tab, aswell as debugging for hours i'm certain that the discard action works, but the two GET requests fired by FE are running on errors.

My guess to what happens is, that the Draft is discarded before the Read triggers, therefore Entity with "isActiveEntity"=false cannot be accessed and the query fails. The weird thing about that is, that this should be dafault Draft Logic and works everywhere else. So i feel like i am missing something. 

Also i am not using @odata.draft.enabled, because that would then use the CAP Default but we have all our data on the RAP Service and need to proxy the requests the way i do (please correct me if i'm wrong here).

Help is greatly appreciated and i will provide any further information you might need.

Cheers, Henrik

entry.title: CAP to BPA Trigger: API returns instance ID, but completely missing in Monitoring/Inbox (Shared Env)
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

I'm facing a weird issue triggering an SAP Build Process Automation (BPA) workflow from my CAP backend.

Everything worked perfectly when the BPA project was deployed in the default Public environment. However, after undeploying and moving it to a newly created Shared environment, the workflow silently disappears.

Here is what is happening:

  • I updated the endpoint URL for the new environment.

  • I generated a new API Key (irpa-api-key) with the required scopes and passed it in the CAP request headers.

  • The CAP POST request is successful—it returns HTTP 201 and I get a valid bpa-instance-id logged in my console.

  • The Issue: The workflow never arrives in "My Inbox". Furthermore, when I search for the exact instance ID in the BPA Monitoring dashboard, it says "No data" (even with all filters like 'Started By' cleared).

Since the API returns an instance ID, the payload is clearly reaching the BPA server. Why is the instance vanishing before it hits the monitoring dashboard or inbox? Could this be a payload schema mismatch in the new environment, or some hidden routing issue?

Any pointers would be hugely appreciated!

Thanks,

Anurag

entry.title: SAP CAP Node.js with AWS RDS PostgreSQL via Private Link — has anyone done this end-to-end?
entry.content:
Hi community,

I'm exploring the setup of an SAP CAP Node.js application on BTP (Cloud Foundry) connecting to an AWS RDS PostgreSQL instance through SAP Private Link Service, and I'd like to hear from anyone who has gone through this.

A few specific questions:

  1. Beyond the Private Link service itself, what else is required on the BTP side to get CAP connecting to RDS? Is a user-provided service with the Private Link hostname enough, or is there anything else needed (tags, bindings, cds.requires config)?
  2. Database schema deployment — does the CAP deploy process (cds deploy) run against RDS through the Private Link tunnel automatically, or does the initial database setup (tables, schema) have to be handled manually on the AWS side before the app can connect?
  3. MTA structure — are you declaring both the privatelink managed service and the RDS credentials as a user-provided-service in mta.yaml, or is there a cleaner pattern you've adopted?
  4. The hostname chicken-and-egg problem — since the Private Link hostname is only available after manual approval in the AWS Console, how are you handling this in your CI/CD pipeline? Two-phase deploy?

Any real-world experience or gotchas would be very appreciated.

Thanks

entry.title: CDS compiler bug for OpenAPI generates invalid count properties for OData and REST services
entry.content:
I faced an issue where CAP generated incorrect OpenAPI specs and the API response which was a bit irritating for my frontend team. Therefore I created a minimal CAP/SQLite reproduction for a count-related OpenAPI issue: https://github.com/purplepenguino/cds-openapi-bug


The service uses a simple Authors/Books model and exposes both OData V4 and REST endpoints.
The generated OpenAPI documents describe collection responses using properties such as:

  • value
  • @count
  • books@count

However, the runtime/ server responses use different formats:

  • OData returns @odata.count and books@odata.count.
  • REST returns a bare array without $count=true.
  • REST returns an object containing count and value when $count=true.
  • REST expanded counts also use books@odata.count.

The generated REST and OData schemas are currently almost identical apart from the server URL, even though the runtime response formats differ. The generated $top schema also does not document the effective limit or a continuation mechanism.

 

Protocol/request Generated OpenAPI spec Actual server response
OData collection with $count=trueObject with value and @countObject with value and @odata.count
OData expansion with $count=truebooks@countbooks@odata.count
REST collection without $count=trueObject with valueBare JSON array
REST collection with $count=trueObject with value and @countObject with value and count
REST expansion with $count=truebooks@countbooks@odata.count

Again, you can find the reproduction in this repo here: https://github.com/purplepenguino/cds-openapi-bug

Environment:
@SAP/cds 10.0.5
@SAP/cds-compiler 7.0.3
@SAP/cds-dk 10.0.7
@cap-js/sqlite 3.1.0
Node.js 24.x

The expected fix would be in the CAP runtime/OpenAPI generation that each protocol’s generated schema accurately describes its actual response format :).

entry.title: sap-messages header texts ignore Accept-Language while the error body is localized (@sap/cds 10.1.1)
entry.content:
CAP Node.js runtime @SAP/cds 10.1.1 (first seen on 10.0.6), Node.js 22.23.2, @cap-js/sqlite 3.1.1, in-memory SQLite.

Messages recorded with req.info, req.warn or req.notify are returned in the sap-messages HTTP header. Their text is always resolved in the server default language; the Accept-Language header of the request is ignored. In the same service an error body (req.error) is localized by Accept-Language, including the framework's own MULTIPLE_ERRORS text, so header and body of one service disagree.

The documentation (Node.js > Events and Requests) says that req.info etc. accept the same arguments as req.reject and that "if an Accept-Language header is present in the request, a localized message is looked up in addition, using the preferred language specified in the header, and used for the message property in the HTTP response". Nothing excludes the header messages.

Minimal reproduction

package.json

{ "name": "probe", "private": true, "dependencies": { "@sap/cds": "^10", "@cap-js/sqlite": "^3" } }

srv/probe.cds

service ProbeService {
  entity Things { key ID : Integer; name : String; }
  action boom() returns String;
  action info() returns String;
}

srv/probe.js

const cds = require('@sap/cds');
module.exports = class ProbeService extends cds.ApplicationService {
  init() {
    this.on('boom', (req) => { req.error(409, 'PROBE_CONFLICT'); req.error(400, 'PROBE_BAD'); });
    this.on('info', (req) => { req.info('PROBE_INFO'); return 'ok'; });
    return super.init();
  }
};

_i18n/messages.properties

PROBE_CONFLICT=EN conflict text
PROBE_BAD=EN bad text
PROBE_INFO=EN info text

_i18n/messages_ru.properties

PROBE_CONFLICT=RU conflict text
PROBE_BAD=RU bad text
PROBE_INFO=RU info text

Start with npx cds serve all --in-memory --port 4099, then:

curl -s -i -X POST localhost:4099/odata/v4/probe/info -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' | grep -i '^sap-messages'
curl -s -i -X POST localhost:4099/odata/v4/probe/info -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept-Language: ru' -d '{}' | grep -i '^sap-messages'
curl -s -X POST localhost:4099/odata/v4/probe/boom -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept-Language: ru' -d '{}'

Actual

The header is identical with and without Accept-Language: ru:

sap-messages: [{"code":"PROBE_INFO","message":"EN info text","numericSeverity":2}]
sap-messages: [{"code":"PROBE_INFO","message":"EN info text","numericSeverity":2}]

The error body of the same service under Accept-Language: ru is localized, including the framework text:

{"error":{"message":"Произошло несколько ошибок, подробности см. ниже.","code":"MULTIPLE_ERRORS","details":[{"message":"RU conflict text","code":"409","@Common.numericSeverity":4},{"message":"RU bad text","code":"400","@Common.numericSeverity":4}],"@Common.numericSeverity":4}}

Expected

sap-messages[].message is RU info text under Accept-Language: ru, consistent with the error body.

Impact and workaround

Success and information messages that SAP Fiori elements shows after an action appear in the server default language for every user. Our workaround: req.info(cds.i18n.messages.at(key, req.locale, args)).

Is this a known issue, or is the header intentionally not localized? If it is intentional, the documentation should say so.

entry.title: Positional req.error(409, 'KEY'): details[].code is "409", not the message key (cds 10.1.1)
entry.content:
CAP Node.js runtime @SAP/cds 10.1.1 (first seen on 10.0.6), Node.js 22.23.2, @cap-js/sqlite 3.1.1, in-memory SQLite.

The positional form req.error(409, 'PROBE_CONFLICT') resolves the text of PROBE_CONFLICT from the i18n bundle, so the second argument is recognised as the message key, but the OData error carries the HTTP status as details[].code ("409"). The object form req.error({ status: 409, code: 'PROBE_CONFLICT' }) with the same intent carries "PROBE_CONFLICT". The status is already the HTTP status of the response, so a code of "409" tells the client nothing, and the message key is lost.

The documentation (Node.js > Events and Requests) lists the positional variant as req.error(status?, message?, target?, args?), says that code is the i18n lookup key and that message is used as the key when code is omitted. It does not say which code the client receives in that case.

Minimal reproduction

package.json

{ "name": "probe", "private": true, "dependencies": { "@sap/cds": "^10", "@cap-js/sqlite": "^3" } }

srv/probe.cds

service ProbeService {
  entity Things { key ID : Integer; name : String; }
  action boomPositional() returns String;
  action boomObject() returns String;
}

srv/probe.js

const cds = require('@sap/cds');
module.exports = class ProbeService extends cds.ApplicationService {
  init() {
    this.on('boomPositional', (req) => {
      req.error(409, 'PROBE_CONFLICT');
      req.error(400, 'PROBE_BAD');
    });
    this.on('boomObject', (req) => {
      req.error({ status: 409, code: 'PROBE_CONFLICT' });
      req.error({ status: 400, code: 'PROBE_BAD' });
    });
    return super.init();
  }
};

_i18n/messages.properties

PROBE_CONFLICT=EN conflict text
PROBE_BAD=EN bad text

Start with npx cds serve all --in-memory --port 4099, then:

curl -s -X POST localhost:4099/odata/v4/probe/boomPositional -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
curl -s -X POST localhost:4099/odata/v4/probe/boomObject -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'

Actual

Positional form:

{"error":{"message":"Multiple errors occurred, see details below.","code":"MULTIPLE_ERRORS","details":[{"message":"EN conflict text","code":"409","@Common.numericSeverity":4},{"message":"EN bad text","code":"400","@Common.numericSeverity":4}],"@Common.numericSeverity":4}}

Object form:

{"error":{"message":"Multiple errors occurred, see details below.","code":"MULTIPLE_ERRORS","details":[{"message":"EN conflict text","code":"PROBE_CONFLICT","@Common.numericSeverity":4},{"message":"EN bad text","code":"PROBE_BAD","@Common.numericSeverity":4}],"@Common.numericSeverity":4}}

With a single error (req.reject(409, 'PROBE_CONFLICT')) the top-level error.code behaves the same way.

Expected

The same handler intent gives the same OData error: details[].code is PROBE_CONFLICT in both forms, or the documentation states that the positional form cannot carry a message code and the status is sent as code.

Impact and workaround

A client that reacts to code (SAP Fiori elements message handling, tests asserting code) cannot use the positional form. Our workaround: the object form only, fixed as a project pattern.

Is the positional form meant to send the status as code, or should details[].code be the message key as in the object form? If the former is intended, could the documentation say so?

entry.title: Navigating to child page error through req.error() target
entry.content:
This is a desensitized example. 

I am attaching the code and the picture. Everything I am doing is in Typescript. 

I have a fiori application where I have a List Report Application and a Child Page Users containing ID, name and email that can be navigated to.
I have the following logic bound with the SAVE hook for the Application after I make changes in the overall application.

this.before('SAVE', 'CatalogService.ParentApp', async (req) => {
  const appId = req.params?.[0]?.ID ?? req.data?.ID
  if (!appId) return

  const data = await SELECT('ID', 'name', 'email')
    .from('CatalogService.Users.drafts')
    .where({ parentApp_ID: appId })

  const isEmail = (s) => /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(String(s || '').trim())

  const badEmail = data.filter(d => !isEmail(d.email));

  for (const d of badEmail) {
     const baseMsg = _tArgs(req, 'err_email', [d.name ?? '?']);
     const msg = `${baseMsg}`;
     const targetPath = `in/users(ID=${d.ID},IsActiveEntity=false)/email`;
     req.error(400, msg, targetPath);
   }
}

My intention for using the target inside req.error was so that it would highlight the email field in the child page (Users)
But instead, it highlights the specific row(s) containing the issue and when I navigate to the child page using the link in the error, the email is not highlighted.

How can I implement it so that it not only highlights from the parent level, but also highlights in the child level? Please give me some ideas on guided error behavior. 

Thank you!
